_doc: Declarative base-node set baked into the from-scratch Fluxbee install.
Single source of truth read by BOTH packaging/build-deb.sh and scripts/install.sh
(they must not diverge), and cross-checked against the sy_orchestrator
TO ADD A NODE TO THE INSTALL: add one entry below (and make sure its crate builds).
singletons: motherbee-only infra nodes run by a packaged systemd unit. NOW EMPTY: IO.blob and
IO.cloud were promoted to first-class MANAGED runtimes (below) so they configure via
CONFIG_SET/GET like every other IO node instead of ENV. They enforce motherbee-only via a
fail-closed self-check in the binary (no systemd ExecCondition anymore).
runtimes: instanced nodes baked into dist/runtimes/<runtime>/<version>, spawnable
per-tenant on demand via run_node. When 'boot': true, fluxbee-firstboot auto-spawns
one default instance ('instance') at the root tenant so it is RUNNING at boot
(degraded/unconfigured until the operator loads its secret/config into SY.vault).
When 'boot': false the runtime is only baked+spawnable, not started.
workspace: cargo manifest dir for the crate; 'go' means a Go binary (see go/).
Growth BEYOND this base set does NOT need a new .deb: publish the runtime and push a
SYSTEM_UPDATE category=runtime over the existing dist-sync/manifest channel.

runtimes._note: io.blob is the motherbee-local public-artifact curator. Promoted from a systemd singleton to a first-class MANAGED runtime: it boots DEGRADED (a curator with default paths + default max_bytes is a valid unconfigured node) and takes config (io.max_bytes / io.admin_hive) via CONFIG_SET/GET, NO env. Motherbee-only is enforced by a fail-closed self-check in the binary. Bare instance name (not .default) because it is a true singleton, not a fanout family.

io.cloud is the in-mesh Fluxbee Cloud provisioning relay. Promoted from a systemd singleton to a first-class MANAGED runtime: it boots DEGRADED (an io.cloud with no trusted edge is valid — it serves the mesh and trusts no edge yet) and takes its single config field io.edge_node via CONFIG_SET/GET, NO env. publish_cloud_endpoint records the edge into this node's config as part of publishing. Motherbee-only via a fail-closed self-check; externalize is admin-driven (io.cloud does NOT self-externalize at boot). Bare instance name (true singleton).

io.slack is instanced (one node per Slack workspace+channel binding; the ICH is derived from (workspace_id, conversation_id)). The boot instance uses the DOTTED name IO.slack.default for the same reason io.wapp does: a family glob 'IO.slack.*@<hive>' would NOT match a bare 'IO.slack'. Additional bindings are spawned per-tenant via run_node (Fluxbee Cloud does it through IO.cloud's provision_node). Inbound is Socket Mode (outbound WebSocket to slack.com), so this node needs NO edge endpoint — only egress to the internet.

io.wapp is fanout (one node per WhatsApp number; all share ONE Meta webhook). The boot instance uses the DOTTED name IO.wapp.default so it matches the externalize-as-fanout family glob 'IO.wapp.*@<hive>' (the bare 'IO.wapp' would NOT match that glob). Additional per-number nodes are spawned as IO.wapp.<label>@<hive> via run_node. Degraded until BOTH its vault secret (resource_type 'whatsapp') is loaded AND the operator externalizes the fanout webhook.

wf.engine (wf-generic) is the WF engine runtime; WF.* nodes are spawned from a WORKFLOW PACKAGE that runs on it, not by run_node on the bare runtime (run_node returns WF_RUNTIME_PACKAGE_REQUIRED). So it ships baked+available but boot=false — publish a workflow package and spawn the WF node when needed.
